observations.statement: SS-020 is an accepted backend requirement in which the `skill` permission key governs skill loading and granular rules address canonical Skill IDs.
SS-021 places permission grants on canonical Skill IDs rather than raw paths and subjects resource disclosure and file operations to FileSafe and external-directory guards.

SS-022 limits child runs to an effective compatible subset of parent-allowed skills, establishes the parent as a capability ceiling, canonicalizes discovered global roots, and rejects symlink escapes.
SS-023 assigns skill management to Agent Config > Skills, retains system-level dependencies in Settings, and makes legacy Settings > Skills a redirect/focus path.
Skill-driven file-tree, evidence-root, restore, and `/revert` flows must carry project/worktree identity and degrade if the target is absent, archived, or no longer current.
The canonical invocation key is `skill_id`; compatibility aliases may be normalized but cannot bypass ID validation, exact-name permission checks, registry lookup, or readiness gating.
The `skill` result is a structured `skill-content` envelope with named required and optional fields, bounded relative resource guidance, and canonical source-vocabulary normalization.
Runtime blocked/recovery contracts use canonical, stable, ordered `allowed_action_ids[]`; `allowed_actions` is only a compatibility label.
The Skills tab is a loaded-skills catalog for discovered, imported, and catalog-installed rows, with a legacy source alias, filters, inspection details, and enumerated badges and flags.
SS-024 requires a store-versus-management split plus import/manage actions, and preserves `Skill Store` and `/install-only` as exact tokens.
SS-025 requires skill rows/cards to distinguish source from location, preserve origin labels and URLs, and show plain-language primary states with remediation text and matched action buttons.

Each of SS-020 through SS-025 prohibits this PlanUnit from creating WorkNodes, queues, production tasks, implementation files, or source code and names plan-migration and plan-index validation surfaces.

candidate_findings.title: Skill permission decision semantics are not defined
candidate_findings.statement: The core says the `skill` permission key supports granular rules over canonical Skill IDs, but it does not define the rule schema, match semantics, wildcard or hierarchy behavior, conflict precedence, default outcome, or structured denial result.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent builders can grant different effective capabilities for the same rules, including over-broad loading or inconsistent denials at a security boundary.

candidate_findings.title: FileSafe and external-directory enforcement lacks an executable decision contract
candidate_findings.statement: SS-021 names canonical IDs, a FileSafe allowlist, external-directory policy, blocked-action recovery, and underlying file operations, but does not specify path-resolution timing, covered operations and disclosures, allowlist matching, rejection codes, recovery payloads, or race-resistant enforcement.
candidate_findings.impact: Resource disclosure and file operations can diverge across implementations or cross the intended external-directory boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Child effective-subset computation is underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The parent ceiling is explicit, but `effective compatible subset` has no defined inputs, compatibility dimensions, set-combination order, evaluation point, snapshot behavior, or response to parent grant and readiness changes during a child run.
candidate_findings.impact: Child runs may receive inconsistent skill sets, retain revoked capability, or be denied valid capability depending on builder choices.

candidate_findings.title: Allowed-root canonicalization and symlink rejection have no lifecycle or failure semantics
candidate_findings.statement: SS-022 requires canonicalized global roots and rejected symlink escapes but does not define normalization rules, nested or changed-link handling, when checks repeat, how discovery continues after rejection, or what failure evidence is returned.
candidate_findings.impact: Different root resolvers can expose different skill resources or handle escape attempts inconsistently, weakening a capability boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Multi-worktree degradation behavior is not operationally defined
candidate_findings.statement: The requirement says flows carry worktree identity and `degrade` for absent, archived, or stale targets, but it does not define the resulting state, which operations become unavailable, whether read-only inspection remains possible, recovery choices, user messaging, or evidence that prevents fallback to another worktree.
candidate_findings.impact: Restore or `/revert` implementations could silently target the wrong worktree, fail opaquely, or expose inconsistent recovery behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Skill invocation and result envelope are not fully typed
candidate_findings.statement: The core identifies the canonical input, compatibility aliases, validation gates, result fields, and optional markers, but does not define field types and cardinalities, unknown-field handling, validation order, failure variants, or whether partial resource samples are deterministic and bounded.
candidate_findings.impact: Tool callers, providers, and GUI consumers can implement incompatible request validation and result/error decoding.

candidate_findings.title: Canonical recovery action vocabulary is named but not enumerated
candidate_findings.statement: `allowed_action_ids[]` is declared stable and ordered for blocked/recovery contracts, yet this core supplies neither the allowed IDs nor their ordering, availability predicates, parameters, or result transitions.
candidate_findings.impact: Runtime and GUI consumers cannot interoperate deterministically on recovery actions and may expose unavailable or unsafe actions.

candidate_findings.title: Redirect, focus, and dependency deep-link behavior remains discretionary
candidate_findings.statement: Ownership is clear, but the legacy redirect/focus target and the conditions and destinations for dependency deep links are described with `where appropriate` and `may`, without exact focus placement, unavailable-target behavior, return navigation, or state preservation.
candidate_findings.impact: The same dependency can lead users to different Settings surfaces or lose navigation context, and focus behavior can be inconsistent.

candidate_findings.title: Catalog filter and badge composition semantics are missing
candidate_findings.statement: The catalog must provide search, source/readiness filters, details, and many badges/flags, but the core does not define filter conjunction and reset behavior, canonical filter values, badge coexistence or precedence, warning-blocked action availability, or loading, empty, and failure states.
candidate_findings.impact: Catalogs can present materially different row sets and conflicting readiness truth for identical data.

candidate_findings.title: Store, import, install, and manage action lifecycles are not specified
candidate_findings.statement: SS-024 states a store-versus-management split and import/manage actions and preserves `/install-only`, but does not define the action inventory, preconditions, confirmation, progress, cancellation, retry, idempotency, failure recovery, or resulting catalog-state transitions.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can create incompatible and potentially duplicate or partially applied skill installation flows.

candidate_findings.title: Provenance and readiness states are lists without deterministic mappings
candidate_findings.statement: SS-025 requires source/location distinction, origin labels and URLs, primary states, remediation text, and matched actions, while the exact-token list enumerates examples but does not map source records or readiness causes to a single state, message, action ID, button availability, or transition.
candidate_findings.impact: The GUI can misstate readiness or provenance and direct users to the wrong remediation even when backend facts are identical.

candidate_findings.title: GUI accessibility behavior has no explicit contract
candidate_findings.statement: The GUI requirements cover redirect/focus, search and filters, badges, details, states, and action buttons, but this core does not specify keyboard order and operation, accessible names, status announcement, non-color state cues, or focus restoration.
candidate_findings.impact: A conforming visual implementation can still be unusable or misleading for keyboard and assistive-technology users.

candidate_findings.title: Acceptance evidence is structural rather than behavioral
candidate_findings.statement: Across SS-020 through SS-025, acceptance checks address PlanUnit addressability, preservation of source material, and prohibition on implementation artifacts, while the named validators are plan-migration and index checks; no exact oracle in this core exercises grant decisions, guarded failures, child inheritance, root rejection, navigation, catalog behavior, or state/action mapping.
candidate_findings.impact: The units can satisfy the stated acceptance blocks while incompatible or unsafe runtime and GUI behavior remains untested.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The permission identity boundary is explicit: grants operate over canonical Skill IDs, not raw filesystem paths.
The child capability ceiling is explicit and repeated as a negative constraint: a child must not exceed the parent ceiling.
The root-security outcome is explicit at a high level: discovered global roots are canonicalized and symlink escapes are rejected.
The GUI authority split is explicit: Agent Config > Skills owns management and Settings retains named system dependencies.
Compatibility invocation aliases explicitly cannot bypass Skill ID validation, exact-name permission checks, registry lookup, or readiness gating.
The result envelope explicitly bounds assistant-visible resource paths to relative paths within FileSafe-permitted skill resources and rejects provider-private injection as a canonical runtime path.
The canonical blocked/recovery field is explicitly `allowed_action_ids[]`, not the legacy `allowed_actions` display label.
The legacy `/imported/catalog-installed` wording is explicitly an alias for source rows rather than a separate source type.
The catalog explicitly must expose browse/search/filter, source/readiness filtering, inspection, validation and warning details, badges, and the listed row flags.
Skill rows/cards explicitly must pair plain-language primary states with remediation text and matched action buttons.
The worktree boundary explicitly forbids assuming a single `active-worktree` and requires active project/worktree identity in context.
The PlanUnit compilation boundary is explicit: these units do not create WorkNodes or implementation artifacts.

unknowns.statement: It is unknown from this window whether PDS-003, PDS-004, PDS-005, PNC-001, or PS-001 defines the missing permission-rule, denial, or FileSafe decision semantics.
It is unknown from this window whether T-001, PLUG-001, SP-001, or the preserved cross-contract dependencies define the compatible-subset algorithm and allowed-root lifecycle.
It is unknown from this window whether the referenced FinalGUISpec and Personas contracts provide exact navigation, accessibility, catalog, provenance, or remediation mappings.
The state model and evidence contract owned by `skill_runtime_readiness` are unknown because this core names that owner but does not define it.
It is unknown whether the named plan-migration and plan-index validators perform behavioral assertions beyond the acceptance prose because their behavior and outputs are not included in this window.

preserved_contractrefs:
- 'ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/FinalGUISpec.md, ContractName:Plans/Personas.md'

- The canonical invocation key is `skill_id`. Legacy or provider-style inputs such as `path_or_name` and `path_or_name -> content, name` MAY be normalized only as compatibility aliases; they do not bypass Skill ID validation, permission checks by exact skill name, registry lookup, or readiness gating.

- 'The `skill` result is a structured `skill-content` envelope: `skill_id`, `title`, `content`, `source_type`, `resource_base_dir?`, `resource_entries_sample?`, and `metadata?`; `name` is a compatibility display alias for `title`. Resource guidance is relative-resource guidance only: assistant-visible paths must be relative to `resource_base_dir` and remain within FileSafe-permitted skill resources. `source_type` uses the canonical source vocabulary below; legacy `built-in` or `/built-in` wording normalizes to `bundled` / PM-bundled, `resource-root` normalizes to `resource_base_dir?`, and provider-private skill injection is not a canonical runtime path.'

- Skill-triggered runtime actions normalize legacy `allowed_actions[]` displays to canonical `allowed_action_ids[]`; `allowed_actions` is a compatibility label, while `allowed_action_ids` is the stable ordered action vocabulary used by runtime blocked/recovery contracts.

- 'Agent Config > Skills is the page-level GUI management surface for agent-management skills. It is not a `settings-only` tab. Legacy `Settings > Skills` copy is a redirect/focus entry into Agent Config > Skills, while Settings remains owner for Authentication, Models/Permissions, permission profiles, rules/commands, runtime controls, and health. Agent Config may cross-link to Settings when a persona or skill depends on those system resources; for example, a blocked provider/account capability may deep-link to Authentication, Health, or `/Models/Permissions` without moving that dependency into Agent Config. Source tokens `/catalog/runtime`, `/discoverability`, and `management-surface` normalize here: Agent Config > Skills is the Skills `/catalog/runtime` and `/discoverability` management-surface for Skill IDs, while runtime readiness remains owned by `skill_runtime_readiness`.'

- The Skills tab is the loaded-skills catalog for discovered, imported, and catalog-installed entries; legacy `/imported/catalog-installed` copy is an alias for those source rows, not a separate source type. It must support browse/search/filter (`/search/filter`), source/readiness (`source-readiness`) filters including `/global/bundled/catalog`, preview/body inspection, validation details, warning details, and source/readiness badges. Rows preserve `referenced_by_persona`, `auto_invokable`, `assistant-auto-usable`, `requires_missing_capability`, `catalog_update_available`, `imported-with-warnings`, and `warning-blocked` badges/flags where applicable.
